steps.title: Three everyday exchanges
body: A1 gave you the basics — greetings, asking where something is, saying please and thank you. A2 puts those together into fuller, more natural exchanges: paying for something, giving directions with more than one landmark, and the small polite phrases that smooth over any request.
مُمْكِن؟ ... طَبْعًا! — a request and an easy "of course" is the shape of most everyday Arabic exchanges.

steps.title: Three exchanges
steps.intro: Tap 🔊 and listen first, before you read. Then reveal the meaning and check what was asked and answered.

steps.title: At the shop
steps.prompt: How much does the item cost?

steps.title: Paying
steps.arabicPrompt: نَقْدٌ أَوْ بِطَاقَةُ اِئْتِمَانٍ؟ — بِطَاقَةُ اِئْتِمَانٍ، مِنْ فَضْلِك.
steps.prompt: How does the customer choose to pay?
steps.explanation: بِطَاقَةُ اِئْتِمَانٍ = "a credit card" — بِطَاقَة (card) + اِئْتِمَان (credit), an iḍāfa.

steps.title: Asking the way
steps.arabicPrompt: أَيْنَ الْبَنْكُ؟ — الْبَنْكُ قَرِيبٌ، بِجَانِبِ الْمَطْعَمِ.
steps.prompt: Where is the bank, according to the passerby?
steps.explanation: بِجَانِبِ الْمَطْعَمِ = "next to the restaurant." The bank is later placed أَمَامَ الْمَكْتَبَةِ (in front of the library), too — two landmarks, not one.

steps.title: You've handled three real exchanges
steps.message: Shopping, asking the way, and a small polite request — the everyday conversations A2 is really for. Every word and phrase here was already in your vocabulary; this lesson just put them to work together.
